item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports metamorphic testing, but the retrieved literature does not establish a ready-made BERT4Rec integrity suite covering all requested defects. A [2024 recommender-testing study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410) evaluates six metamorphic relations across LibRec, PREA and Surprise; its findings do not directly validate Transformer masking or padding probes. A [2025 mutation-testing study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107807), on optimisation software, offers a transferable method: assess relations against deliberately faulty implementations and measure sensitivity across test inputs. BERT4Rec’s [replicability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483) establishes the relevant contract: masked-item training with bidirectional attention and appended-mask inference; shifted targets can expose answers through bidirectional context.\n\nSuggested application, inferred from these sources: instrument the actual sampler to record source interaction positions, corruption positions, targets, split provenance and RNG state. Validate these records against public training histories; repeated item IDs alone do not prove leakage. Inject isolated defects—restore a supervised masked token, shift mask/label alignment, replace final-position readout with count−1 on unequal left-padded histories, or alter the exported predictor’s weights/item mapping. Record which assertions detect each mutant, alongside clean controls and explicit detection denominators. Compare in-memory and exported-predictor candidate scores in evaluation mode on identical inputs. These checks measure sensitivity to specified faults; synthetic successes do not certify the real pipeline. Certification claims require evidence that the same probes exercise the actual sampler, trained model and exported predictor."}
